# Прямой файловый доступ к роботу по SFTP

## Context

**Что случилось.** 2026-08-07 приложение `reachy_mini_conversation_app` на роботе падало с `exit 1`: личность
`Test_Ru` была создана в старом формате (`instructions.txt` + `tools.txt` + …), а приложение обновилось до версии,
читающей только `profile.md`. Выбор профиля лежит в `startup_settings.json` **внутри** каталога пакета в
`/venvs/apps_venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<package>/` — это runtime-файл в install prefix, поэтому
`pip uninstall` его не удаляет и переустановка не помогает. Settings-UI приложения на `:7860` тоже недоступен: его
подаёт сам процесс приложения, который падает до того, как поднимет страницу. Починка потребовала SSH руками.

**Почему это не лечится через daemon API.** В `Sources/ReachyKit/openapi.json` 77 путей, среди них ни одного,
пишущего произвольный файл (`media/sounds/upload` кладёт только звук по имени, `kinematics/stl` — чтение). Это не
пробел в спеке, а сознательная граница демона. Значит клиенту нужен файловый путь **сбоку** от демона.

**Что делаем.** Файловый менеджер робота по SFTP внутри приложения — для продвинутых пользователей, на iOS и macOS,
только по LAN.

## Что уже есть и переделывать не нужно

Треть исходного ТЗ (`/Users/aleksei/Developer/Reachy_mini/docs/2026-08-07-reachy-mini-swift-direct-ssh-design.md`)
описывает существующий код. Ничего из этого в план не входит:

| Пункт ТЗ | Уже реализовано |
| --- | --- |
| Тейл `journalctl` | `Transport/LogStreamClient.swift` (`/logs/ws/daemon`), `Central/RemoteDaemonLog.swift`, `LogConsoleScreen` |
| Рестарт демона / приложения | `POST /api/daemon/restart`, `/api/apps/{restart-current-app,start-app,stop-current-app}`, `Session/RobotPower.swift` |
| Видно, что приложение упало | `Apps/RunningAppCaption.swift` печатает stderr-хвост |
| Settings-UI приложения | `Apps/AppSettingsScreen.swift` |

Следствие: **открытый вопрос ТЗ «есть ли беспарольный sudo для `systemctl`» снимается** — рестарт идёт через демон,
SSH для него не нужен, и `exec` в транспорте не требуется вообще.

- **Свой экран, а не File Provider extension.** Ни iOS Files, ни Finder не говорят по SFTP (Files умеет только SMB;

- **Мастер починки профиля — отдельным спеком.** Файловый экран уже позволяет починить `profile.md` руками.

линкует `ReachyWidgetUI`. SSH внутри `ReachyKit` заставил бы процесс, разбуженный нарисовать две строки текста,

подаёт сам процесс приложения, который падает до того, как поднимет страницу. Починка потребовала SSH руками.

**Почему это не лечится через daemon API.** В `Sources/ReachyKit/openapi.json` 77 путей, среди них ни одного,
пишущего произвольный файл (`media/sounds/upload` кладёт только звук по имени, `kinematics/stl` — чтение). Это не
пробел в спеке, а сознательная граница демона. Значит клиенту нужен файловый путь **сбоку** от демона.

**Что делаем.** Файловый менеджер робота по SFTP внутри приложения — для продвинутых пользователей, на iOS и macOS,
только по LAN.

## Что уже есть и переделывать не нужно

Треть исходного ТЗ (`/Users/aleksei/Developer/Reachy_mini/docs/2026-08-07-reachy-mini-swift-direct-ssh-design.md`)
описывает существующий код. Ничего из этого в план не входит:

| Пункт ТЗ | Уже реализовано |
| --- | --- |
| Тейл `journalctl` | `Transport/LogStreamClient.swift` (`/logs/ws/daemon`), `Central/RemoteDaemonLog.swift`, `LogConsoleScreen` |
| Рестарт демона / приложения | `POST /api/daemon/restart`, `/api/apps/{restart-current-app,start-app,stop-current-app}`, `Session/RobotPower.swift` |
| Видно, что приложение упало | `Apps/RunningAppCaption.swift` печатает stderr-хвост |
| Settings-UI приложения | `Apps/AppSettingsScreen.swift` |

Следствие: **открытый вопрос ТЗ «есть ли беспарольный sudo для `systemctl`» снимается** — рестарт идёт через демон,
SSH для него не нужен, и `exec` в транспорте не требуется вообще.

## Принятые решения

- **Свой экран, а не File Provider extension.** Ни iOS Files, ни Finder не говорят по SFTP (Files умеет только SMB;
  Finder — SMB/AFP/NFS/WebDAV). Системная интеграция потребовала бы `NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension`, включения
  App Sandbox на macOS-таргете (сейчас его нет), второго App ID и ручной регистрации App Group через Xcode.
- **Без встроенного редактора.** Правка = скачать → поправить внешним редактором → залить поверх. Поэтому загрузка
  обязана уметь **заменить конкретный файл**, а не только положить новый в каталог.
- **Без запуска команд и без PTY.** Логи и рестарт уже на стороне демона.
- **Мастер починки профиля — отдельным спеком.** Файловый экран уже позволяет починить `profile.md` руками.
- **Только LAN.** `RobotSession.address` отдаёт `nil` для relay-сессии; по ADR 0003 релей несёт WebRTC, а не TCP.

## Архитектура

### Новый продукт `ReachySSH`

**Почему отдельный продукт, а не папка в `ReachyKit`:** `ReachyWidgetUI` зависит от `ReachyKit`, а виджет-расширение
линкует `ReachyWidgetUI`. SSH внутри `ReachyKit` заставил бы процесс, разбуженный нарисовать две строки текста,
линковать SwiftNIO. Тот же аргумент, которым в репозитории обоснована граница `ReachyMedia`.

`ReachySSH` **не зависит** от `ReachyKit` — хост, порт и креды приходят значениями, как токен приходит в `ReachyKit`
из `HuggingFaceAuth`.

```
ReachySSH (Foundation + Citadel)  ──►  ReachyUI
ReachyKit ──► ReachyWidgetUI ──► виджет      (SwiftNIO сюда не попадает)
```

Файлы в `Sources/ReachySSH/`:

| Файл | Содержимое |
| --- | --- |
| `RemoteFile.swift` | value type: `name`, `path`, `kind` (file/directory/symlink), `size`, `modified`, `permissions` |
| `RobotFileSystem.swift` | протокол: `list`, `read`, `write`, `makeDirectory`, `remove`, `rename`, `attributes` |
| `SSHFileSystem.swift` | `actor`, реализация поверх Citadel |
| `SSHCredentials.swift`, `KeychainSSHCredentialStore.swift` | пользователь + пароль |
| `HostKeyFingerprint.swift`, `KeychainHostKeyStore.swift` | пиннинг host key |
| `TOFUHostKeyValidator.swift` | `NIOSSHClientServerAuthenticationDelegate` |
| `ReachySSHError.swift` | типизированный enum |
| `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` (симлинк) | по конвенции репозитория |

`Package.swift`: новый `.library` + `.target` с `exclude: ["AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"]`, зависимость
`https://github.com/orlandos-nl/Citadel`, новый `.testTarget(name: "ReachySSHTests")`, и `ReachySSH` в зависимостях
`ReachyUI`.

### UI

Новый каталог `Sources/ReachyUI/Files/`:

- `RobotFilesModel.swift` — `@MainActor @Observable`. Держит стек пути, `entries`, фазу («ещё не отвечал» отдельно от
  «пусто» — иначе первый кадр соврёт), `lastError`, подтверждения. `#if DEBUG` фабрики превью в этом же файле
  (по `ReachyUI/AGENTS.md` они пишут `private` члены, куда `@testable` не достаёт).
- `RobotFilesScreen.swift` — список, breadcrumb, тулбар (New Folder, Upload), контекстное меню на строке
  (Download, Replace…, Rename, Delete), `contentLoading(isPresented:title:)` на первую загрузку,
  `ContentUnavailableView` на пустой каталог и на ошибку.
- `RemoteFileRow.swift`, `RobotFilesAccessSheet.swift` (креды + подтверждение отпечатка).
- `Sources/ReachyUI/Previews/RobotFilesPreviews.swift`.

`Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`: новая `filesSection` **между** `diagnosticsSection` и `privacySection`, под гейтом
`isConnectedOverLAN`. Не в `recoverySection` — её футер обещает «робот отвалился от сети, нужна Bluetooth-близость», а
SSH требует ровно обратного; это та же логика, по которой `diagnosticsSection` намеренно лежит выше «Advanced».

### Тесты

- `Tests/ReachySSHTests/` — форматирование отпечатка (OpenSSH `SHA256:<base64 без padding>`), сборка путей, маппинг
  ошибок, конечный автомат TOFU. Всё чистые функции.
- `Tests/ReachyUITests/RobotFilesModelTests.swift` — против `StubRobotFileSystem` в `ReachyTestSupport`.
- По правилу 7: никаких `Task.sleep` перед ассертами, поллинг условий, `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))` на асинхронные.

## Ключевые точки реализации

1. **TOFU — это два подключения, а не запрос в середине рукопожатия.** Citadel отдаёт
   `NIOSSHClientServerAuthenticationDelegate.validateHostKey` с `EventLoopPromise`, который обязан ответить
   синхронно и не может дождаться пользователя. Поэтому: первая попытка идёт с валидатором, который знает
   запиннный ключ, если он есть. Если ключа нет — валидатор **запоминает предъявленный и падает** с
   `.hostKeyUnknown(fingerprint)`. UI показывает отпечаток, пользователь подтверждает, второе подключение идёт с
   `SSHHostKeyValidator.trustedKeys([key])`. Сменившийся ключ — `.hostKeyChanged(expected:actual:)` и требует явного
   повторного доверия.

2. **Оба секрета ключуются по `RobotIdentity.hardwareID`** (с откатом на `deduplicationKey`, т.к. на симуляторе
   `hardwareID` равен `nil`), никогда по адресу — правило 4. Адрес робота меняется от сети к сети, host key нет.
   Keychain-элементы `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, форма как у
   `HuggingFaceAuth/KeychainHFTokenStore.swift`.

3. **Типы Citadel не покидают актора.** `SSHFileSystem` — `actor`, который владеет `SSHClient`/`SFTPClient` и наружу
   отдаёт только value types. Это верно независимо от того, `Sendable` они или нет; **`Sendable` их не проверял** —
   это как раз то, что должен установить спайк (риск 1), и от ответа зависит, нужен ли где-то `@unchecked`.

4. **Своя `describe`, а не `recordDaemonFailure`.** Это не вызовы демона — тот же случай, что `OnboardingModel` (BLE)
   и `HFSignInModel` (`ASWebAuthenticationSession`). Отмену всё равно надо отфильтровать: пользователь, ушедший с
   экрана посреди листинга, не должен получить красную ошибку.

5. **Корень энумерации — `/`**, плюс строки-закладки на `/venvs/apps_venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages` и
   `/home/pollen`. Без path jail: аудитория — продвинутые пользователи, а jail это код, который может только ошибаться.

6. **Каждое деструктивное действие за `confirmationDialog`**, описание над кнопкой — как в `MaintenanceCard`. Удаление
   непустого каталога в v1 отклоняется, а не рекурсируется.

7. **`read` отдаёт `Data` с потолком (8 MiB) и `.tooLarge` выше него** — телефон не должен молча тянуть в память
   двухгигабайтный файл модели. Скачивание пишет во временный файл и отдаёт в `.fileExporter`, загрузка читает из
   `.fileImporter`.

8. **Не наступить на задокументированный зависон компилятора.** По корневому `CLAUDE.md`: замыкание, вложенное в
   builder `AsyncStream { continuation in … }` и захватывающее escaping-continuation, роняет SIL-проход
   `ClosureLifetimeFixup` в невозвратный обход доминаторов — 20+ минут одного ядра без диагностики. Прогресс передачи,
   если понадобится, делать плоским `@Sendable (Double) -> Void`, а не вложенным стримом.

9. **Строки** — только `.reachy(_:)` (правило 9). Осторожно с ключами, различающимися одной пунктуацией: пара вида
   `Delete file` / `Delete file?` — это жёсткая ошибка сборки `xcstringstool`, а не предупреждение (прецедент
   `Remove every app?` в `MaintenanceCard`).

10. **Превью пишутся так, чтобы их тела не называли ни одного типа из `ReachySSH`** — тогда `Apps/.prefire.yml`
    не меняется вовсе. Prefire копирует тело превью в генерируемый файл, который импортирует только список
    `testable_imports`; если тип из `ReachySSH` всё же попадёт в тело, `ReachySSH` придётся добавить в **оба**
    блока `testable_imports`.

## Риски

1. **Citadel под Swift 6 strict concurrency на пиннутом тулчейне.** Сначала спайк одним файлом: собрать
   `SSHClient.connect` + `openSFTP` + `listDirectory` и убедиться, что это компилируется и не требует `@unchecked`
   в нашем коде. Откат на голый `swift-nio-ssh` означает писать подсистему SFTP самим — это другая оценка целиком,
   и знать об этом надо до, а не после написания UI.
2. **`Package.resolved` вырастет далеко за 16 пинов** (Citadel тянет swift-nio, swift-nio-ssh, swift-crypto,
   swift-collections, swift-log). Строку корневого `CLAUDE.md` про «коммить 16-пиновую версию» надо обновить тем же
   коммитом, иначе она превращается в ловушку.
3. **Эталоны снапшотов на несвязанных экранах могут поехать.** По `CLAUDE.md` это бывает от сдвига тайминга прогона,
   когда среди превью есть неопределённый `ProgressView` (а он тут будет — «подключаемся», «передаём»). Перед
   принятием широкой правки сверить один эталон, на который ничто не могло повлиять (`JoystickPad`), с HEAD.
4. **macOS-таргет сейчас несандбоксный**, поэтому делать ничего не нужно. Если App Sandbox когда-нибудь включат,
   исходящему SSH понадобится `com.apple.security.network.client`.

## Порядок работ

1. Спайк Citadel (риск 1). Если не проходит — остановиться и пересмотреть план.
2. `ReachySSH`: value types, протокол, ошибки, отпечаток, Keychain-хранилища, TOFU-валидатор, актор. Тесты чистых частей.
3. `StubRobotFileSystem` в `ReachyTestSupport`; `RobotFilesModel` + его тесты.
4. Экраны, лист, контекстное меню, sheet кредов/отпечатка, `filesSection` в настройках.
5. Строки в `ReachyDesign/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`.
6. Превью, `mise run project`, запись эталонов, `git add` PNG.
7. `AGENTS.md` для `ReachySSH`; правка строки про пины в корневом `CLAUDE.md`.

## Verification

```bash
./bin/mise run build
./bin/mise run test
./bin/mise run lint
./bin/mise run format-check
./bin/mise run build:app          # macOS
./bin/mise run build:app:ios      # единственный, что компилирует виджет
./bin/mise run project
./bin/mise run test:snapshots     # прочитать список поехавших
./bin/mise run test:snapshots:record
```

**Дешёвый прогон UI без робота:** включить на Mac Remote Login и указать приложению адрес хоста, где крутится
`mise run sim-daemon` — получается настоящий SFTP-сервер для всего экрана. Отдельно проверить, что при **выключенном**
Remote Login экран показывает внятную ошибку, а не висит.

**Прогон на живом роботе** (`./bin/mise run device`):

- запиннить host key, прочитать отпечаток;
- один раз ввести неверный пароль — увидеть `.authenticationFailed`, а не общую сетевую ошибку;
- дойти до `/venvs/apps_venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`, скачать `profile.md`, залить обратно поверх, убедиться,
  что содержимое изменилось (`ssh pollen@<robot> cat …`);
- mkdir, rename, delete на своём тестовом каталоге; отказ на удалении непустого;
- открыть большой файл модели — увидеть `.tooLarge`, а не рост памяти;
- подключиться через релей и убедиться, что секция скрыта.

**После работы** погасить `sim-daemon` и симуляторы.

1. **Citadel под Swift 6 strict concurrency на пиннутом тулчейне.** Сначала спайк одним файлом: собрать
   `SSHClient.connect` + `openSFTP` + `listDirectory` и убедиться, что это компилируется и не требует `@unchecked`

input.new_string:
## Результаты спайка (риск 1 закрыт)

Спайк: `scratchpad/citadel-spike`, Citadel 0.9.2, Swift 6.3, `.swiftLanguageMode(.v6)` → `Build complete`, ноль
предупреждений. Девять находок, три из которых меняют дизайн:

1. **`extension SSHClient: @retroactive @unchecked Sendable {}` обязателен, а не опционален.** `SSHClient` —
   non-Sendable `final class`; созданный внутри async-функции, он «task-isolated» и **не может быть сохранён никуда
   разделяемое**. Проверены и отвергнуты: `actor` со стороннимй свойством (`sending 'client' risks causing data
   races`), `nonisolated(unsafe)` (не помогает — ошибка на локальной переменной), `Mutex<SSHClient?>`
   (`'inout sending' parameter cannot be task-isolated`). Обоснование конформанса: Citadel помечает `Sendable` тот
   `SFTPClient`, который сам же и выдаёт, а оба гоняются через один и тот же NIO `Channel`. Если Citadel однажды
   добавит conformance сам — получим ошибку сборки, не тихий баг.
2. **`ReachySSH` обязан владеть одним долгоживущим `MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup`** и передавать его в каждый
   `connect`. Дефолт Citadel — `group: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup = .init(numberOfThreads: 1)`, то есть новая группа
   на каждое подключение, а `close()` закрывает только канал и **группу не гасит**. `SSHClient` при этом не имеет
   `deinit` вообще. Итого: утечка потока на каждое переподключение — а на нестабильном LAN их много.
3. **SFTP-сессию открывать один раз на подключение, а не на операцию.** `openSFTP()` создаёт дочерний канал плюс
   round trip и сам логирует предупреждение «Likely the result of opening too many SFTPClient handles».
4. **Host key round-trip есть, и он текстовый:** `String(openSSHPublicKey: key)` ⇄
   `NIOSSHPublicKey(openSSHPublicKey: string)`. Значит в Keychain кладём строку `"ssh-ed25519 AAAA…"`, а не блоб.
5. **Отпечаток считается без NIOSSH.** `String(openSSHPublicKey:)` base64-кодирует ровно тот wire-формат, который
   OpenSSH хеширует. То есть `SHA256:` + base64(SHA256(base64Decode(второе поле))) без `=` — Foundation + CryptoKit
   и ничего больше. Полностью юнит-тестируемо известным вектором.
6. **Тип файла лежит в битах S_IFMT поля `permissions`** (`0o040000` каталог, `0o120000` симлинк, `0o100000` файл) —
   отдельного поля вида в SFTP нет. `longname.first == "d"` — единственный откат, если сервер не отдал permissions.
7. `remove` (файл) и `rmdir` (каталог) — раздельные вызовы, поэтому отказ на непустом каталоге приходит от сервера
   бесплатно, без нашей проверки.
8. **Citadel тянет не Apple'овский `swift-nio-ssh`, а форк `Joannis/swift-nio-ssh` 0.3.5.** Это меняет профиль риска:
   откат «взять swift-nio-ssh напрямую» — не drop-in замена.
9. `SSHHostKeyValidator` живёт в Citadel (`ClientSession.swift:154`), не в NIOSSH, и предлагает
   `.trustedKeys(Set<NIOSSHPublicKey>)` / `.custom(delegate)` / `.acceptAnything()`; отказ — `InvalidHostKey`.
   TOFU-делегат — `final class … : Sendable` с `Mutex<String?>`; `validateHostKey` вызывается на потоке event loop.

## Риски

1. ~~Citadel под Swift 6 strict concurrency~~ — закрыт спайком, см. выше.
2. **`Package.resolved`: 16 → 25 пинов.** Новые девять: `citadel`, `swift-nio`, `swift-nio-ssh`, `swift-crypto`,
   `swift-log`, `swift-atomics`, `swift-system`, `bigint`, `colorizeswift`; пересечение только по
   `swift-collections`. Строку корневого `CLAUDE.md` про «коммить 16-пиновую версию» обновить тем же коммитом, иначе
   она превращается в ловушку. Холодная сборка — 481 задача: swift-crypto тащит vendored BoringSSL, Citadel — bcrypt
   на C.

   `connect`. Дефолт Citadel — `group: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup = .init(numberOfThreads: 1)`, то есть новая группа

   `deinit` вообще. Итого: утечка потока на каждое переподключение — а на нестабильном LAN их много.

input.content:
# ReachySSH

SFTP to the robot, for the files the daemon API deliberately cannot reach. Foundation + Citadel, no UI imports,
Swift 6 strict concurrency.

**Why this is its own product and not a corner of `ReachyKit`.** `ReachyWidgetUI` depends on `ReachyKit`, and the
widget extension links `ReachyWidgetUI`. SSH inside `ReachyKit` would make a process woken for a moment to draw two
lines of text link SwiftNIO. Same argument the repository already made for `ReachyMedia`, applied to a different
dependency. `ReachySSH` knows nothing about robots either: host, port and credentials arrive as values, the way a
Hugging Face token reaches `ReachyKit` from `HuggingFaceAuth`.

## What is deliberately absent

- **No `exec`, no PTY.** The daemon already tails `journalctl` (`/logs/ws/daemon`, `LogStreamClient`) and already
  restarts itself and its apps (`POST /api/daemon/restart`, `/api/apps/restart-current-app`). Adding a command
  runner here would duplicate a supported surface and put robot control on a path that bypasses project rule 2.
  It also settles the question of whether `pollen` has passwordless `sudo`: it does not matter, nothing needs it.
- **No text editor.** Editing is download → change on the device → upload over the same path, so `write` truncates
  and creates. That is why the upload flow has to offer "replace this file" and not only "add a file here".
- **No recursion.** `remove` picks `remove` or `rmdir` from the entry's kind, and `rmdir` refuses a non-empty
  directory. The server's refusal *is* the guard; do not add a recursive delete.
- **No relay support.** SSH needs a TCP route to port 22, and the Hugging Face relay carries WebRTC (ADR 0003).
  `RobotSession.address` answers nil for a remote session, which is what closes the feature.

## Citadel, and the four things it made us do

Pinned `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.9.2")` — it is pre-1.0, where a minor bump is a breaking change, unlike the `from:`
every other dependency uses. It resolves **`Joannis/swift-nio-ssh`, a fork**, not Apple's `swift-nio-ssh`: the
fallback "just use swift-nio-ssh directly" is not a drop-in, and this fork is one person's.

1. **`extension SSHClient: @retroactive @unchecked Sendable {}` is required, not tidying.** Citadel marks the
   `SFTPClient` it hands out `Sendable` but not the `SSHClient` that opened it, though both are driven through the
   same NIO `Channel`. An `SSHClient` built inside an `async` function is therefore task-isolated and **cannot be
   stored anywhere shared at all.** Measured, not guessed — all three alternatives fail:
   | Attempt | Diagnostic |
   | --- | --- |
   | actor stored property | `sending 'client' risks causing data races` |
   | `nonisolated(unsafe) var client` | same — the diagnostic lands on the *local*, not the property |
   | `Mutex<SSHClient?>` | `'inout sending' parameter '$0' cannot be task-isolated at end of function` |
   If Citadel ever declares the conformance itself this becomes a duplicate-conformance build error. Loud, one line.
2. **Pass `MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup.singleton` to every `connect`.** Citadel's default parameter is
   `group: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup = .init(numberOfThreads: 1)` — a fresh group per connection — and `close()`
   closes the channel without shutting the group down. `SSHClient` has no `deinit` at all. So the default leaks one
   thread per reconnect, and a flaky LAN reconnects a lot.
3. **Open the SFTP subsystem once per connection.** `openSFTP()` costs a child channel plus a round trip and logs
   its own warning about "too many SFTPClient handles". `SSHFileSystem` holds the one it opened.
4. **TOFU is two connections, because it has to be.** `validateHostKey` must resolve an `EventLoopPromise` during
   the handshake; there is no way to suspend it while a person reads a fingerprint. So `TOFUHostKeyValidator`
   **records the offered key and refuses**; `mapConnectFailure` reads that record — not the thrown error, which NIO
   wraps — to tell `hostKeyUnknown` from `hostKeyChanged`. The screen shows it, the user accepts, the key is pinned,
   the second connection succeeds. Citadel's own `InvalidHostKey` is public with an internal initialiser, hence the
   private `HostKeyRefused` sentinel.

## Facts about SFTP this layer encodes

- **There is no field for what kind of thing an entry is.** It lives in the `S_IFMT` bits of `permissions`
  (`0o040000` directory, `0o120000` symlink, `0o100000` file). `RemoteFile.kind(mode:longname:)` reads those and
  falls back to `longname`'s first character — the `ls -l` one — only when a server sent no permissions.
- **`permissions` is a bare `UInt32`.** `RemoteFile.permissionsText` renders `drwxr-xr-x` from it rather than
  reusing `longname`, which is the server's own rendering and varies between implementations.
- **There is no "directory not empty" status code.** OpenSSH answers a plain `failure` and puts the reason in the
  human-readable `message`, so that string is what `map` has to match on. Fragile by nature; it degrades to
  `.transport` rather than lying.
- `accessModificationTime.modificationTime` is already a `Date`, not the `UInt32` the wire format carries.
- `.` and `..` come back in every listing and are filtered here, once, rather than in each screen.

## Credentials and keys

Both live in the Keychain, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, in the shape
`KeychainHFTokenStore` established — written against `Security` directly, because the whole surface is three calls
and a dependency holding a credential is one more thing to audit.

- **Keyed by the robot's hardware id, never by its address** (project rule 4). A robot moves between networks; its
  host key does not. `RobotIdentity.hardwareID` is nil on the simulator, so callers pass `deduplicationKey`.
- **The pinned key is stored as its OpenSSH text line**, not as an opaque blob:
  `String(openSSHPublicKey:)` ⇄ `NIOSSHPublicKey(openSSHPublicKey:)` is a documented round-trip, and a layout that
  belongs to a dependency has no business in a Keychain item.
- **`KeychainSSHCredentialStore` stores username and password only.** Host and port are the session's business; a
  remembered address is exactly the mistake rule 4 warns about, so `credentials(forRobot:)` returns an empty host
  for the caller to fill.
- **The fingerprint needs no SwiftNIO.** The base64 field of an OpenSSH line *is* the SSH wire encoding, which is
  what OpenSSH hashes, so `HostKeyFingerprint` is Foundation plus one SHA-256 — and its tests use vectors from
  `ssh-keygen -lf`, not from this code. A trailing comment is dropped, or one key would pin as two.

## Defaults, and why they are only defaults

Reachy Mini Wireless ships with OpenSSH enabled, user `pollen`, password `root`. `SSHCredentials.defaultUsername`
offers the username as a prefill. Never assume the password: a user who takes the advice to change it must still be
able to connect. Say so on the screen.

## Testing

`Tests/ReachySSHTests` covers only what is pure — fingerprints, the mode→kind mapping, permission rendering, path
joining, error classification. There is **no integration test against a live SSH server**, and the cheap way to
exercise the real actor is to enable Remote Login on the Mac and point the app at it: that is a genuine OpenSSH
server for the price of a checkbox. `PreviewFileSystem` (in `Preview/`, `#if DEBUG`, the same convention as
`ReachyKit/Preview/PreviewRobotClient`) is what previews and the UI model's tests run against; it records calls in
order, so "did it even ask?" is assertable. It is here rather than in `ReachyTestSupport` so no other test target
links SwiftNIO.

`PreviewFileSystem.brokenPersonality()` is the 2026-08-07 incident as a fixture: `user_personalities/Test_Ru` in
the old four-file format with no `profile.md`. Keep it broken — it is the state the feature exists for.

# ReachySSH

SFTP to the robot, for the files the daemon API deliberately cannot reach. Foundation + Citadel, no UI imports,
Swift 6 strict concurrency.

**Why this is its own product and not a corner of `ReachyKit`.** `ReachyWidgetUI` depends on `ReachyKit`, and the
widget extension links `ReachyWidgetUI`. SSH inside `ReachyKit` would make a process woken for a moment to draw two
lines of text link SwiftNIO. Same argument the repository already made for `ReachyMedia`, applied to a different
dependency. `ReachySSH` knows nothing about robots either: host, port and credentials arrive as values, the way a
Hugging Face token reaches `ReachyKit` from `HuggingFaceAuth`.

## What is deliberately absent

- **No `exec`, no PTY.** The daemon already tails `journalctl` (`/logs/ws/daemon`, `LogStreamClient`) and already
  restarts itself and its apps (`POST /api/daemon/restart`, `/api/apps/restart-current-app`). Adding a command
  runner here would duplicate a supported surface and put robot control on a path that bypasses project rule 2.
  It also settles the question of whether `pollen` has passwordless `sudo`: it does not matter, nothing needs it.
- **No text editor.** Editing is download → change on the device → upload over the same path, so `write` truncates
  and creates. That is why the upload flow has to offer "replace this file" and not only "add a file here".
- **No recursion.** `remove` picks `remove` or `rmdir` from the entry's kind, and `rmdir` refuses a non-empty
  directory. The server's refusal *is* the guard; do not add a recursive delete.
- **No relay support.** SSH needs a TCP route to port 22, and the Hugging Face relay carries WebRTC (ADR 0003).
  `RobotSession.address` answers nil for a remote session, which is what closes the feature.

## Citadel, and the four things it made us do

Pinned `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.9.2")` — it is pre-1.0, where a minor bump is a breaking change, unlike the `from:`
every other dependency uses. It resolves **`Joannis/swift-nio-ssh`, a fork**, not Apple's `swift-nio-ssh`: the
fallback "just use swift-nio-ssh directly" is not a drop-in, and this fork is one person's.

1. **`extension SSHClient: @retroactive @unchecked Sendable {}` is required, not tidying.** Citadel marks the
   `SFTPClient` it hands out `Sendable` but not the `SSHClient` that opened it, though both are driven through the
   same NIO `Channel`. An `SSHClient` built inside an `async` function is therefore task-isolated and **cannot be
   stored anywhere shared at all.** Measured, not guessed — all three alternatives fail:
   | Attempt | Diagnostic |
   | --- | --- |
   | actor stored property | `sending 'client' risks causing data races` |
   | `nonisolated(unsafe) var client` | same — the diagnostic lands on the *local*, not the property |
   | `Mutex<SSHClient?>` | `'inout sending' parameter '$0' cannot be task-isolated at end of function` |
   If Citadel ever declares the conformance itself this becomes a duplicate-conformance build error. Loud, one line.
2. **Pass `MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup.singleton` to every `connect`.** Citadel's default parameter is
   `group: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup = .init(numberOfThreads: 1)` — a fresh group per connection — and `close()`
   closes the channel without shutting the group down. `SSHClient` has no `deinit` at all. So the default leaks one
   thread per reconnect, and a flaky LAN reconnects a lot.
3. **Open the SFTP subsystem once per connection.** `openSFTP()` costs a child channel plus a round trip and logs
   its own warning about "too many SFTPClient handles". `SSHFileSystem` holds the one it opened.
4. **TOFU is two connections, because it has to be.** `validateHostKey` must resolve an `EventLoopPromise` during
   the handshake; there is no way to suspend it while a person reads a fingerprint. So `TOFUHostKeyValidator`
   **records the offered key and refuses**; `mapConnectFailure` reads that record — not the thrown error, which NIO
   wraps — to tell `hostKeyUnknown` from `hostKeyChanged`. The screen shows it, the user accepts, the key is pinned,
   the second connection succeeds. Citadel's own `InvalidHostKey` is public with an internal initialiser, hence the
   private `HostKeyRefused` sentinel.

## Facts about SFTP this layer encodes

- **There is no field for what kind of thing an entry is.** It lives in the `S_IFMT` bits of `permissions`
  (`0o040000` directory, `0o120000` symlink, `0o100000` file). `RemoteFile.kind(mode:longname:)` reads those and
  falls back to `longname`'s first character — the `ls -l` one — only when a server sent no permissions.
- **`permissions` is a bare `UInt32`.** `RemoteFile.permissionsText` renders `drwxr-xr-x` from it rather than
  reusing `longname`, which is the server's own rendering and varies between implementations.
- **There is no "directory not empty" status code.** OpenSSH answers a plain `failure` and puts the reason in the
  human-readable `message`, so that string is what `map` has to match on. Fragile by nature; it degrades to
  `.transport` rather than lying.
- `accessModificationTime.modificationTime` is already a `Date`, not the `UInt32` the wire format carries.
- `.` and `..` come back in every listing and are filtered here, once, rather than in each screen.

## Credentials and keys

Both live in the Keychain, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, in the shape
`KeychainHFTokenStore` established — written against `Security` directly, because the whole surface is three calls
and a dependency holding a credential is one more thing to audit.

- **Keyed by the robot's hardware id, never by its address** (project rule 4). A robot moves between networks; its
  host key does not. `RobotIdentity.hardwareID` is nil on the simulator, so callers pass `deduplicationKey`.
- **The pinned key is stored as its OpenSSH text line**, not as an opaque blob:
  `String(openSSHPublicKey:)` ⇄ `NIOSSHPublicKey(openSSHPublicKey:)` is a documented round-trip, and a layout that
  belongs to a dependency has no business in a Keychain item.
- **`KeychainSSHCredentialStore` stores username and password only.** Host and port are the session's business; a
  remembered address is exactly the mistake rule 4 warns about, so `credentials(forRobot:)` returns an empty host
  for the caller to fill.
- **The fingerprint needs no SwiftNIO.** The base64 field of an OpenSSH line *is* the SSH wire encoding, which is
  what OpenSSH hashes, so `HostKeyFingerprint` is Foundation plus one SHA-256 — and its tests use vectors from
  `ssh-keygen -lf`, not from this code. A trailing comment is dropped, or one key would pin as two.

## Defaults, and why they are only defaults

Reachy Mini Wireless ships with OpenSSH enabled, user `pollen`, password `root`. `SSHCredentials.defaultUsername`
offers the username as a prefill. Never assume the password: a user who takes the advice to change it must still be
able to connect. Say so on the screen.

## Testing

`Tests/ReachySSHTests` covers only what is pure — fingerprints, the mode→kind mapping, permission rendering, path
joining, error classification. There is **no integration test against a live SSH server**, and the cheap way to
exercise the real actor is to enable Remote Login on the Mac and point the app at it: that is a genuine OpenSSH
server for the price of a checkbox. `PreviewFileSystem` (in `Preview/`, `#if DEBUG`, the same convention as
`ReachyKit/Preview/PreviewRobotClient`) is what previews and the UI model's tests run against; it records calls in
order, so "did it even ask?" is assertable. It is here rather than in `ReachyTestSupport` so no other test target
links SwiftNIO.

`PreviewFileSystem.brokenPersonality()` is the 2026-08-07 incident as a fixture: `user_personalities/Test_Ru` in
the old four-file format with no `profile.md`. Keep it broken — it is the state the feature exists for.

content.subject: Explore project context for SSH/file-access spec
content.description: Read the external spec, Package.swift, Apps/Project.swift, ReachyKit/ReachyUI layout, daemon OpenAPI surface, existing Recovery/Apps/Settings screens and git history. Establish what the spec asks for that already exists.

content.subject: Ask clarifying questions one at a time
content.description: Understand purpose, constraints and success criteria: which part of the spec is actually wanted, scope of File Provider, auth model, platform priority.

content.subject: Propose 2-3 approaches with trade-offs
content.description: Compare: full ReachySSH + File Provider; targeted SSH recovery only; daemon-only / robot-side maintenance app. Give a recommendation.

content.subject: Spike: Citadel under Swift 6 strict concurrency
content.description: Isolated scratch package on the pinned toolchain: SSHClient.connect + openSFTP + listDirectory. Establish whether it compiles in Swift 6 language mode and whether SSHClient/SFTPClient are Sendable. Blocking: if it fails, stop and revisit the plan.

content.subject: Build ReachySSH target
content.description: Value types, RobotFileSystem protocol, typed errors, host key fingerprint, Keychain stores for credentials and pinned key, TOFU validator, SSHFileSystem actor. Unit tests for the pure parts. Package.swift wiring + AGENTS.md.

content.subject: Build the files screen and wire it into Settings
content.description: StubRobotFileSystem in ReachyTestSupport, RobotFilesModel + tests, RobotFilesScreen, RemoteFileRow, RobotFilesAccessSheet, filesSection in SettingsScreen, strings, previews + recorded snapshots.

5	// The robot's own file system over SFTP — the one screen that reaches the robot
6	// without the daemon, because the daemon has no route that writes a file.

8	// The fixture is the 2026-08-07 incident: `user_personalities/Test_Ru` left in the
9	// old four-file format with no `profile.md`, which is what made the conversation app
10	// exit 1 before it could serve the settings page that would have fixed it.

14	#Preview("Robot files — password") {
15	    PreviewScene.robotFiles(.preview(phase: .needsPassword, password: ""))
16	}
17	
18	// A refused password goes back to the field rather than to a dead end, and the
19	// stored one is dropped — keeping it means the next visit fails identically.
20	#Preview("Robot files — password refused") {
21	    PreviewScene.robotFiles(
22	        .preview(
23	            phase: .needsPassword,

25	            password: ""

27	    )
28	}

30	// Trust on first use. The key is shown before it is pinned, because pinning it
31	// silently would make the pin worthless.

34	}

37	// does this — and so does someone sitting in the middle.
38	#Preview("Robot files — identity changed") {

content.content:
# ReachySSH

SFTP to the robot, for the files the daemon API deliberately cannot reach. Foundation + Citadel, no UI imports,
Swift 6 strict concurrency.

**Why this is its own product and not a corner of `ReachyKit`.** `ReachyWidgetUI` depends on `ReachyKit`, and the
widget extension links `ReachyWidgetUI`. SSH inside `ReachyKit` would make a process woken for a moment to draw two
lines of text link SwiftNIO. Same argument the repository already made for `ReachyMedia`, applied to a different
dependency. `ReachySSH` knows nothing about robots either: host, port and credentials arrive as values, the way a
Hugging Face token reaches `ReachyKit` from `HuggingFaceAuth`.

## What is deliberately absent

- **No `exec`, no PTY.** The daemon already tails `journalctl` (`/logs/ws/daemon`, `LogStreamClient`) and already
  restarts itself and its apps (`POST /api/daemon/restart`, `/api/apps/restart-current-app`). Adding a command
  runner here would duplicate a supported surface and put robot control on a path that bypasses project rule 2.
  It also settles the question of whether `pollen` has passwordless `sudo`: it does not matter, nothing needs it.
- **No text editor.** Editing is download → change on the device → upload over the same path, so `write` truncates
  and creates. That is why the upload flow has to offer "replace this file" and not only "add a file here".
- **No recursion.** `remove` picks `remove` or `rmdir` from the entry's kind, and `rmdir` refuses a non-empty
  directory. The server's refusal _is_ the guard; do not add a recursive delete.
- **No relay support.** SSH needs a TCP route to port 22, and the Hugging Face relay carries WebRTC (ADR 0003).
  `RobotSession.address` answers nil for a remote session, which is what closes the feature.

## Citadel, and the four things it made us do

Pinned `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.9.2")` — it is pre-1.0, where a minor bump is a breaking change, unlike the `from:`
every other dependency uses. It resolves **`Joannis/swift-nio-ssh`, a fork**, not Apple's `swift-nio-ssh`: the
fallback "just use swift-nio-ssh directly" is not a drop-in, and this fork is one person's.

Adding it also introduced **four `ld:` warnings that are not ours and cannot be fixed here**:
`building for macOS-11.0, but linking with dylib '/usr/lib/swift/libswiftCore.dylib' which was built for newer
version 13.0`, ×4. They come from `CitadelServerExample`, an executable target inside Citadel that `swift build`
compiles along with everything else, and from `ColorizeSwift`, which declares no `platforms:` at all and so falls
back to SwiftPM's ancient default. `mise run build` still reports `status: success` and CI has no
warnings-as-errors policy. Do not go hunting for them in this target — there is nothing here to change.

1. **`extension SSHClient: @retroactive @unchecked Sendable {}` is required, not tidying.** Citadel marks the
   `SFTPClient` it hands out `Sendable` but not the `SSHClient` that opened it, though both are driven through the
   same NIO `Channel`. An `SSHClient` built inside an `async` function is therefore task-isolated and **cannot be
   stored anywhere shared at all.** Measured, not guessed — all three alternatives fail:
   | Attempt                                                                                                           | Diagnostic                                                                  |
   | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | actor stored property                                                                                             | `sending 'client' risks causing data races`                                 |
   | `nonisolated(unsafe) var client`                                                                                  | same — the diagnostic lands on the _local_, not the property                |
   | `Mutex<SSHClient?>`                                                                                               | `'inout sending' parameter '$0' cannot be task-isolated at end of function` |
   | If Citadel ever declares the conformance itself this becomes a duplicate-conformance build error. Loud, one line. |                                                                             |
2. **Pass `MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup.singleton` to every `connect`.** Citadel's default parameter is
   `group: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup = .init(numberOfThreads: 1)` — a fresh group per connection — and `close()`
   closes the channel without shutting the group down. `SSHClient` has no `deinit` at all. So the default leaks one
   thread per reconnect, and a flaky LAN reconnects a lot.
3. **Open the SFTP subsystem once per connection.** `openSFTP()` costs a child channel plus a round trip and logs
   its own warning about "too many SFTPClient handles". `SSHFileSystem` holds the one it opened.
4. **TOFU is two connections, because it has to be.** `validateHostKey` must resolve an `EventLoopPromise` during
   the handshake; there is no way to suspend it while a person reads a fingerprint. So `TOFUHostKeyValidator`
   **records the offered key and refuses**; `mapConnectFailure` reads that record — not the thrown error, which NIO
   wraps — to tell `hostKeyUnknown` from `hostKeyChanged`. The screen shows it, the user accepts, the key is pinned,
   the second connection succeeds. Citadel's own `InvalidHostKey` is public with an internal initialiser, hence the
   private `HostKeyRefused` sentinel.

## Facts about SFTP this layer encodes

- **There is no field for what kind of thing an entry is.** It lives in the `S_IFMT` bits of `permissions`
  (`0o040000` directory, `0o120000` symlink, `0o100000` file). `RemoteFile.kind(mode:longname:)` reads those and
  falls back to `longname`'s first character — the `ls -l` one — only when a server sent no permissions.
- **`permissions` is a bare `UInt32`.** `RemoteFile.permissionsText` renders `drwxr-xr-x` from it rather than
  reusing `longname`, which is the server's own rendering and varies between implementations.
- **There is no "directory not empty" status code.** OpenSSH answers a plain `failure` and puts the reason in the
  human-readable `message`, so that string is what `map` has to match on. Fragile by nature; it degrades to
  `.transport` rather than lying.
- `accessModificationTime.modificationTime` is already a `Date`, not the `UInt32` the wire format carries.
- `.` and `..` come back in every listing and are filtered here, once, rather than in each screen.

## Credentials and keys

Both live in the Keychain, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, in the shape
`KeychainHFTokenStore` established — written against `Security` directly, because the whole surface is three calls
and a dependency holding a credential is one more thing to audit.

- **Keyed by the robot's hardware id, never by its address** (project rule 4). A robot moves between networks; its
  host key does not. `RobotIdentity.hardwareID` is nil on the simulator, so callers pass `deduplicationKey`.
- **The pinned key is stored as its OpenSSH text line**, not as an opaque blob:
  `String(openSSHPublicKey:)` ⇄ `NIOSSHPublicKey(openSSHPublicKey:)` is a documented round-trip, and a layout that
  belongs to a dependency has no business in a Keychain item.
- **`KeychainSSHCredentialStore` stores username and password only.** Host and port are the session's business; a
  remembered address is exactly the mistake rule 4 warns about, so `credentials(forRobot:)` returns an empty host
  for the caller to fill.
- **The fingerprint needs no SwiftNIO.** The base64 field of an OpenSSH line _is_ the SSH wire encoding, which is
  what OpenSSH hashes, so `HostKeyFingerprint` is Foundation plus one SHA-256 — and its tests use vectors from
  `ssh-keygen -lf`, not from this code. A trailing comment is dropped, or one key would pin as two.

## Defaults, and why they are only defaults

Reachy Mini Wireless ships with OpenSSH enabled, user `pollen`, password `root`. `SSHCredentials.defaultUsername`
offers the username as a prefill. Never assume the password: a user who takes the advice to change it must still be
able to connect. Say so on the screen.

## Testing

`Tests/ReachySSHTests` covers only what is pure — fingerprints, the mode→kind mapping, permission rendering, path
joining, error classification. There is **no integration test against a live SSH server**, and the cheap way to
exercise the real actor is to enable Remote Login on the Mac and point the app at it: that is a genuine OpenSSH
server for the price of a checkbox. `PreviewFileSystem` (in `Preview/`, `#if DEBUG`, the same convention as
`ReachyKit/Preview/PreviewRobotClient`) is what previews and the UI model's tests run against; it records calls in
order, so "did it even ask?" is assertable. It is here rather than in `ReachyTestSupport` so no other test target
links SwiftNIO.

`PreviewFileSystem.brokenPersonality()` is the 2026-08-07 incident as a fixture: `user_personalities/Test_Ru` in
the old four-file format with no `profile.md`. Keep it broken — it is the state the feature exists for.

content.subject: Build ReachySSH target

content.subject: Build the files screen and wire it into Settings
content.description: StubRobotFileSystem in ReachyTestSupport, RobotFilesModel + tests, RobotFilesScreen, RemoteFileRow, RobotFilesAccessSheet, filesSection in SettingsScreen, strings, previews + recorded snapshots.

feat(files): browse and change the robot's own files over SFTP

The daemon has no route that writes an arbitrary file — 77 paths, and the only
two that touch storage are a sound upload by name and an STL read. That gap is
what left the 2026-08-07 incident unfixable from the app: a personality left in
the old four-file format made the conversation app exit 1, the profile choice
lives in `startup_settings.json` inside the package directory in `apps_venv`
where `pip uninstall` never looks, and the settings page that would have fixed
it is served by the process that was crashing. Recovery took SSH by hand.

So the app now reaches the file system directly, beside the daemon rather than
through it, for advanced users on the LAN.

- `ReachySSH`: a new product, SFTP over Citadel. Beside `ReachyKit`, not inside
  it — `ReachyWidgetUI` depends on `ReachyKit`, so SSH there would drag SwiftNIO
  into a process woken for a moment to draw two lines of text. Host, port and
  credentials arrive as values; it knows nothing about robots.
- Passwords and pinned host keys in the Keychain, `ThisDeviceOnly`, keyed by the
  robot's hardware id and never by its address (rule 4).
- Trust on first use, in two connections because `validateHostKey` has to resolve
  its promise mid-handshake and cannot wait for a person. A changed key is its
  own state and is never accepted quietly.
- Settings is restructured: Network, Maintenance, Daemon logs, Robot files,
  Recovery over Bluetooth and Developer tools now sit under one Advanced group.
  The group's footer used to promise Bluetooth range, which stopped being true
  the moment it held anything but the BLE console.

Deliberately absent, each for a reason written down in `ReachySSH/AGENTS.md`: no
`exec` or PTY (the daemon already tails journalctl and restarts its own apps, so
whether `pollen` has passwordless sudo stops mattering), no in-app editor
(download, edit on the device, upload over the same path), no recursive delete
(`rmdir` refusing a non-empty directory is the guard), and no relay support
(SSH needs TCP to port 22; the relay carries WebRTC — ADR 0003).

The File Provider extension the original brief asked for is not here and should
not be assumed cheap: neither iOS Files nor Finder speaks SFTP, so system
integration means a replicated extension plus App Sandbox on the macOS target,
a second App ID and a hand-registered App Group.

Verified: 901 unit tests, 303 snapshot references, both app builds, lint and
format clean. Package.resolved goes 16 → 25 pins; the note in AGENTS.md that
named the old count is updated with it.
EOF

content.text:
Готово. Установлено и запущено на iPhone.

## Что сделано

**`ReachySSH`** — новый SPM-продукт: SFTP поверх Citadel 0.9.2. Отдельно от `ReachyKit`, потому что `ReachyWidgetUI` зависит от `ReachyKit`, а виджет линкует `ReachyWidgetUI` — SSH внутри `ReachyKit` затащил бы SwiftNIO в процесс, разбуженный нарисовать две строки. Пароли и запиннные host key в Keychain (`ThisDeviceOnly`), ключуются по hardware id, не по адресу.

**Экран файлов** в `ReachyUI/Files/`: навигация, закладки (корень, `site-packages`, home), скачать, залить, заменить конкретный файл, переименовать, удалить, mkdir. Плюс TOFU-подтверждение отпечатка и отдельное состояние для сменившегося ключа.

**Настройки перестроены** как договорились: Network, Maintenance, Daemon logs, Robot files, Recovery over Bluetooth, Developer tools — всё под одной группой Advanced.

## Проверено

| Гейт | Результат |
|---|---|
| `mise run test` | 901 тест |
| `mise run test:snapshots` | 303 эталона, 0 ошибок |
| `build:app` / `build:app:ios` | оба success, 0 warnings |
| swiftlint --strict / actionlint / format-check | чисто |
| `mise run device` | `App installed:` + `Launched application` |

## Чего я **не** проверил, и это важно

**Ни один байт не прошёл по проводу.** `SSHFileSystem` — реальный путь — ни разу не исполнялся: тесты гоняют `PreviewFileSystem`, а интеграционного теста против живого SSH-сервера нет. API Citadel я сверял по исходникам, не по работе. Значит чек-лист из плана (запиннить ключ, неверный пароль, дойти до `site-packages`, скачать и залить `profile.md` поверх, mkdir/rename/delete, отказ на большом файле) остаётся невыполненным — приложение на телефоне, но прогнать это может только человек рядом с роботом.

Самый дешёвый способ снять этот риск без робота: включить на Mac Remote Login и указать приложению адрес Mac — получится настоящий OpenSSH-сервер за один чекбокс.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Спайк оправдал себя не тем, что нашёл, а тем, чего не дал сделать.** Citadel не помечает `SSHClient` как `Sendable`, и в Swift 6 такой объект, созданный внутри async-функции, нельзя сохранить **вообще никуда** — я перебрал три способа (актор, `nonisolated(unsafe)`, `Mutex`), каждый дал свою ошибку. Напиши я сначала UI, а транспорт потом — и упёрся бы в это, имея вокруг готовые экраны.

**Две находки спайка были бы утечками в проде.** Дефолт Citadel создаёт новый event loop group на каждый `connect`, а `close()` его не гасит и `deinit` у клиента нет — поток на каждое переподключение. И `openSFTP()` на каждую операцию, против чего библиотека предупреждает в своём же логе. Оба факта видны только в исходниках, ни один не следует из документации.

**Один эталон я записал, посмотрел и выбросил.** «Advanced expanded» через `SettingsScreen` отрендерился с группой ниже сгиба — то есть четыре картинки, не удостоверяющие ничего, но читающиеся как покрытие. Вынес секцию в свою вьюху и снял отдельно; теперь строка `Robot files` действительно видна на эталоне, а на релейном — действительно отсутствует.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Два коммита на ветке `feat/robot-files-over-sftp`. Не пушил и PR не открывал — скажите, если нужно.

Из исходного ТЗ я сознательно не делал File Provider (ни Files, ни Finder не говорят по SFTP, это отдельный проект с сэндбоксом на macOS), редактор, запуск команд и мастер починки профиля — последний остался отдельным спеком, как вы и выбрали.

input.command:
gh pr create --title "feat(files): browse and change the robot's own files over SFTP" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

The daemon has no route that writes an arbitrary file. 77 paths, and the only two that touch storage are a sound upload by name and an STL read. That gap is what left the **2026-08-07 incident** unfixable from the app:

- a personality left in the old four-file format made `reachy_mini_conversation_app` exit 1;
- the profile choice lives in `startup_settings.json` **inside** the package directory in `apps_venv`, a runtime file in an install prefix, so `pip uninstall` never removes it and reinstalling does not help;
- the settings page that would have fixed it is served by the process that was crashing.

Recovery took SSH by hand. So the app now reaches the file system directly, beside the daemon rather than through it, for advanced users on the LAN.

## What

**`ReachySSH`** — a new product, SFTP over Citadel. Beside `ReachyKit`, not inside it: `ReachyWidgetUI` depends on `ReachyKit` and the widget extension links `ReachyWidgetUI`, so SSH there would drag SwiftNIO into a process woken for a moment to draw two lines of text. The same argument the repo already made for `ReachyMedia`. It knows nothing about robots — host, port and credentials arrive as values.

**The screen** — navigate, bookmarks (root, `site-packages`, home), download, upload, replace a specific file, rename, delete, mkdir. Trust on first use with the fingerprint shown before it is pinned, and a changed key as its own state that is never accepted quietly.

**Settings restructured** — Network, Maintenance, Daemon logs, Robot files, Recovery over Bluetooth and Developer tools now sit under one Advanced group. Its footer used to promise Bluetooth range, which stopped being true the moment the group held anything but the BLE console.

## Deliberately absent

Each with the reasoning written into `Sources/ReachySSH/AGENTS.md`:

- **No `exec`, no PTY.** The daemon already tails `journalctl` and restarts its own apps, so whether `pollen` has passwordless `sudo` stops mattering — that open question from the brief is closed, not deferred.
- **No in-app editor.** Download, edit on the device, upload over the same path. That is why the row menu offers *Replace* as well as *Download*.
- **No recursive delete.** `rmdir` refusing a non-empty directory is the guard.
- **No relay support.** SSH needs TCP to port 22; the relay carries WebRTC (ADR 0003). `RobotSession.address` is nil for a remote session, which is what hides the row.
- **No File Provider extension**, and it should not be assumed cheap: neither iOS Files nor Finder speaks SFTP, so system integration means a replicated extension plus App Sandbox on the macOS target, a second App ID and a hand-registered App Group.
- **No profile-repair wizard.** Separate spec; the screen already lets you fix `profile.md` by hand, which is what was done over SSH.

## Three things Citadel forced, each measured rather than guessed

1. **`extension SSHClient: @retroactive @unchecked Sendable {}` is required.** Citadel marks the `SFTPClient` it hands out `Sendable` but not the `SSHClient` that opened it, though both run on the same NIO `Channel`. A client built inside an `async` function is task-isolated and cannot be stored anywhere shared: an actor property gives `sending 'client' risks causing data races`, `nonisolated(unsafe)` moves the diagnostic to the local, and `Mutex<SSHClient?>` gives `'inout sending' parameter cannot be task-isolated`.
2. **Pass `MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup.singleton` to every `connect`.** Citadel's default builds a fresh single-thread group per connection, `close()` never shuts one down, and `SSHClient` has no `deinit` — a leaked thread per reconnect.
3. **Open the SFTP subsystem once per connection.** Each `openSFTP()` costs a child channel plus a round trip, and the library logs its own warning about too many handles.

Also worth knowing: Citadel resolves **`Joannis/swift-nio-ssh`, a fork**, not Apple's. `Package.resolved` goes 16 → 25 pins and the note in `AGENTS.md` naming the old count is updated with it.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `mise run test` | 901 passed |
| `mise run test:snapshots` | 303 references, 0 errors |
| `mise run build:app` / `build:app:ios` | success, 0 warnings |
| swiftlint --strict, actionlint, format-check | clean |
| `mise run device` | installed and launched on an iPhone |

Snapshot movement is accounted for: 13 new `Robot files` previews, 4 new `Advanced` ones, and exactly 8 modified — `Settings — Lite robot` and `Settings — backend stopped`, the two references where the lower half of Settings is in frame. Nothing unrelated moved.

An `Advanced — expanded` reference taken through `SettingsScreen` was recorded, inspected and thrown away: the group renders below the fold on both snapshot devices, so those images certified nothing while reading as coverage. The section is now its own view and is captured standalone, which is what makes the `Robot files` row visible in a reference at all — and provably absent in `Advanced — over the relay`.

## Not verified

**No byte has crossed a wire.** `SSHFileSystem` — the real path — has never executed: the tests drive `PreviewFileSystem`, and there is no integration test against a live SSH server. Citadel's API was checked against its sources, not against a running robot. The on-device functional pass is therefore still open:

- [ ] pin the host key, read the fingerprint
- [ ] one wrong password → `.authenticationFailed`, not a generic network error
- [ ] browse to `/venvs/apps_venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`, download `profile.md`, upload it back over the same path, confirm with `ssh pollen@<robot> cat …`
- [ ] mkdir / rename / delete; refusal on a non-empty folder
- [ ] open a large model file → `.tooLarge`, not memory growth
- [ ] connect over the relay and confirm the row is hidden

Cheapest way to exercise the real actor without a robot: enable Remote Login on the Mac and point the app at it — a genuine OpenSSH server for the price of a checkbox.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

[ "$install" = true ] || exit 0

# devicectl prints "Failed to load provisioning paramter list … No provider was found." on
# every invocation and succeeds anyway, so its stderr says nothing about the outcome.
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$core_id" "$PRODUCT"

[ "$launch" = true ] || exit 0

bundle_id="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleIdentifier' "$PRODUCT/Info.plist")"

# A locked phone refuses the launch and nothing else: the new build is already installed,
# so the whole run is one home-screen tap from done. Say that instead of the CoreDevice
# wall of text, and still exit non-zero — the app is not running.
launch_log="$(mktemp -t reachy-launch)"
trap 'rm -f "$devices_json" "$launch_log"' EXIT
if ! xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$core_id" "$bundle_id" 2>&1 | tee "$launch_log"; then
  if grep -q "could not be, unlocked" "$launch_log"; then
    echo "" >&2
    echo "$bundle_id is installed; the phone was locked, so it could not be started." >&2
    echo "Unlock it and rerun, or just tap the icon." >&2
  fi
  exit 3
fi

# Code Review Reception

## Overview

Code review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.

**Core principle:** Verify before implementing. Ask before assuming. Technical correctness over social comfort.

## The Response Pattern

```
WHEN receiving code review feedback:

1. READ: Complete feedback without reacting
2. UNDERSTAND: Restate requirement in own words (or ask)
3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality
4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?
5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback
6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each
```

## Forbidden Responses

**NEVER:**
- "You're absolutely right!" (explicit instruction-file violation)
- "Great point!" / "Excellent feedback!" (performative)
- "Let me implement that now" (before verification)

**INSTEAD:**
- Restate the technical requirement
- Ask clarifying questions
- Push back with technical reasoning if wrong
- Just start working (actions > words)

## Handling Unclear Feedback

```
IF any item is unclear:
  STOP - do not implement anything yet
  ASK for clarification on unclear items

WHY: Items may be related. Partial understanding = wrong implementation.
```

**Example:**
```
your human partner: "Fix 1-6"
You understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.

❌ WRONG: Implement 1,2,3,6 now, ask about 4,5 later
✅ RIGHT: "I understand items 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before proceeding."
```

## Source-Specific Handling

### From your human partner
- **Trusted** - implement after understanding
- **Still ask** if scope unclear
- **No performative agreement**
- **Skip to action** or technical acknowledgment

### From External Reviewers
```
BEFORE implementing:
  1. Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase?
  2. Check: Breaks existing functionality?
  3. Check: Reason for current implementation?
  4. Check: Works on all platforms/versions?
  5. Check: Does reviewer understand full context?

IF suggestion seems wrong:
  Push back with technical reasoning

IF can't easily verify:
  Say so: "I can't verify this without [X]. Should I [investigate/ask/proceed]?"

IF conflicts with your human partner's prior decisions:
  Stop and discuss with your human partner first
```

**your human partner's rule:** "External feedback - be skeptical, but check carefully"

## YAGNI Check for "Professional" Features

```
IF reviewer suggests "implementing properly":
  grep codebase for actual usage

  IF unused: "This endpoint isn't called. Remove it (YAGNI)?"
  IF used: Then implement properly
```

**your human partner's rule:** "You and reviewer both report to me. If we don't need this feature, don't add it."

## Implementation Order

```
FOR multi-item feedback:
  1. Clarify anything unclear FIRST
  2. Then implement in this order:
     - Blocking issues (breaks, security)
     - Simple fixes (typos, imports)
     - Complex fixes (refactoring, logic)
  3. Test each fix individually
  4. Verify no regressions
```

## When To Push Back

Push back when:
- Suggestion breaks existing functionality
- Reviewer lacks full context
- Violates YAGNI (unused feature)
- Technically incorrect for this stack
- Legacy/compatibility reasons exist
- Conflicts with your human partner's architectural decisions

**How to push back:**
- Use technical reasoning, not defensiveness
- Ask specific questions
- Reference working tests/code
- Involve your human partner if architectural

**If you're uncomfortable pushing back out loud:** Name that tension, then tell your partner about the issue you've seen. They'll appreciate your honesty.

## Acknowledging Correct Feedback

When feedback IS correct:
```
✅ "Fixed. [Brief description of what changed]"
✅ "Good catch - [specific issue]. Fixed in [location]."
✅ [Just fix it and show in the code]

❌ "You're absolutely right!"
❌ "Great point!"
❌ "Thanks for catching that!"
❌ "Thanks for [anything]"
❌ ANY gratitude expression
```

**Why no thanks:** Actions speak. Just fix it. The code itself shows you heard the feedback.

**If you catch yourself about to write "Thanks":** DELETE IT. State the fix instead.

## Gracefully Correcting Your Pushback

If you pushed back and were wrong:
```
✅ "You were right - I checked [X] and it does [Y]. Implementing now."
✅ "Verified this and you're correct. My initial understanding was wrong because [reason]. Fixing."

❌ Long apology
❌ Defending why you pushed back
❌ Over-explaining
```

State the correction factually and move on.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Performative agreement | State requirement or just act |
| Blind implementation | Verify against codebase first |
| Batch without testing | One at a time, test each |
| Assuming reviewer is right | Check if breaks things |
| Avoiding pushback | Technical correctness > comfort |
| Partial implementation | Clarify all items first |
| Can't verify, proceed anyway | State limitation, ask for direction |

## Real Examples

**Performative Agreement (Bad):**
```
Reviewer: "Remove legacy code"
❌ "You're absolutely right! Let me remove that..."
```

**Technical Verification (Good):**
```
Reviewer: "Remove legacy code"
✅ "Checking... build target is 10.15+, this API needs 13+. Need legacy for backward compat. Current impl has wrong bundle ID - fix it or drop pre-13 support?"
```

**YAGNI (Good):**
```
Reviewer: "Implement proper metrics tracking with database, date filters, CSV export"
✅ "Grepped codebase - nothing calls this endpoint. Remove it (YAGNI)? Or is there usage I'm missing?"
```

**Unclear Item (Good):**
```
your human partner: "Fix items 1-6"
You understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.
✅ "Understand 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before implementing."
```

## GitHub Thread Replies

When replying to inline review comments on GitHub, reply in the comment thread (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{id}/replies`), not as a top-level PR comment.

# ReachySSH

SFTP to the robot, for the files the daemon API deliberately cannot reach. Foundation + Citadel, no UI imports,
Swift 6 strict concurrency.

**Why this is its own product and not a corner of `ReachyKit`.** `ReachyWidgetUI` depends on `ReachyKit`, and the
widget extension links `ReachyWidgetUI`. SSH inside `ReachyKit` would make a process woken for a moment to draw two
lines of text link SwiftNIO. Same argument the repository already made for `ReachyMedia`, applied to a different
dependency. `ReachySSH` knows nothing about robots either: host, port and credentials arrive as values, the way a
Hugging Face token reaches `ReachyKit` from `HuggingFaceAuth`.

## What is deliberately absent

- **No `exec`, no PTY.** The daemon already tails `journalctl` (`/logs/ws/daemon`, `LogStreamClient`) and already
  restarts itself and its apps (`POST /api/daemon/restart`, `/api/apps/restart-current-app`). Adding a command
  runner here would duplicate a supported surface and put robot control on a path that bypasses project rule 2.
  It also settles the question of whether `pollen` has passwordless `sudo`: it does not matter, nothing needs it.
- **No text editor.** Editing is download → change on the device → upload over the same path, so `write` truncates
  and creates. That is why the upload flow has to offer "replace this file" and not only "add a file here".
- **No recursion.** `remove` picks `remove` or `rmdir` from the entry's kind, and `rmdir` refuses a non-empty
  directory. The server's refusal _is_ the guard; do not add a recursive delete.
- **No relay support.** SSH needs a TCP route to port 22, and the Hugging Face relay carries WebRTC (ADR 0003).
  `RobotSession.address` answers nil for a remote session, which is what closes the feature.

## Citadel, and the four things it made us do

Pinned `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.9.2")` — it is pre-1.0, where a minor bump is a breaking change, unlike the `from:`
every other dependency uses. It resolves **`Joannis/swift-nio-ssh`, a fork**, not Apple's `swift-nio-ssh`: the
fallback "just use swift-nio-ssh directly" is not a drop-in, and this fork is one person's.

Adding it also introduced **four `ld:` warnings that are not ours and cannot be fixed here**:
`building for macOS-11.0, but linking with dylib '/usr/lib/swift/libswiftCore.dylib' which was built for newer
version 13.0`, ×4. They come from `CitadelServerExample`, an executable target inside Citadel that `swift build`
compiles along with everything else, and from `ColorizeSwift`, which declares no `platforms:` at all and so falls
back to SwiftPM's ancient default. `mise run build` still reports `status: success` and CI has no
warnings-as-errors policy. Do not go hunting for them in this target — there is nothing here to change.

1. **`extension SSHClient: @retroactive @unchecked Sendable {}` is required, not tidying.** Citadel marks the
   `SFTPClient` it hands out `Sendable` but not the `SSHClient` that opened it, though both are driven through the
   same NIO `Channel`. An `SSHClient` built inside an `async` function is therefore task-isolated and **cannot be
   stored anywhere shared at all.** Measured, not guessed — all three alternatives fail:
   | Attempt                                                                                                           | Diagnostic                                                                  |
   | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | actor stored property                                                                                             | `sending 'client' risks causing data races`                                 |
   | `nonisolated(unsafe) var client`                                                                                  | same — the diagnostic lands on the _local_, not the property                |
   | `Mutex<SSHClient?>`                                                                                               | `'inout sending' parameter '$0' cannot be task-isolated at end of function` |
   | If Citadel ever declares the conformance itself this becomes a duplicate-conformance build error. Loud, one line. |                                                                             |
2. **Pass `MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup.singleton` to every `connect`.** Citadel's default parameter is
   `group: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup = .init(numberOfThreads: 1)` — a fresh group per connection — and `close()`
   closes the channel without shutting the group down. `SSHClient` has no `deinit` at all. So the default leaks one
   thread per reconnect, and a flaky LAN reconnects a lot.
3. **Open the SFTP subsystem once per connection.** `openSFTP()` costs a child channel plus a round trip and logs
   its own warning about "too many SFTPClient handles". `SSHFileSystem` holds the one it opened.
4. **TOFU is two connections, because it has to be.** `validateHostKey` must resolve an `EventLoopPromise` during
   the handshake; there is no way to suspend it while a person reads a fingerprint. So `TOFUHostKeyValidator`
   **records the offered key and refuses**; `mapConnectFailure` reads that record — not the thrown error, which NIO
   wraps — to tell `hostKeyUnknown` from `hostKeyChanged`. The screen shows it, the user accepts, the key is pinned,
   the second connection succeeds. Citadel's own `InvalidHostKey` is public with an internal initialiser, hence the
   private `HostKeyRefused` sentinel.

## Facts about SFTP this layer encodes

- **There is no field for what kind of thing an entry is.** It lives in the `S_IFMT` bits of `permissions`
  (`0o040000` directory, `0o120000` symlink, `0o100000` file). `RemoteFile.kind(mode:longname:)` reads those and
  falls back to `longname`'s first character — the `ls -l` one — only when a server sent no permissions.
- **`permissions` is a bare `UInt32`.** `RemoteFile.permissionsText` renders `drwxr-xr-x` from it rather than
  reusing `longname`, which is the server's own rendering and varies between implementations.
- **There is no "directory not empty" status code.** OpenSSH answers a plain `failure` and puts the reason in the
  human-readable `message`, so that string is what `map` has to match on. Fragile by nature; it degrades to
  `.transport` rather than lying.
- `accessModificationTime.modificationTime` is already a `Date`, not the `UInt32` the wire format carries.
- `.` and `..` come back in every listing and are filtered here, once, rather than in each screen.

## Credentials and keys

Both live in the Keychain, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, in the shape
`KeychainHFTokenStore` established — written against `Security` directly, because the whole surface is three calls
and a dependency holding a credential is one more thing to audit.

- **Keyed by the robot's hardware id, never by its address** (project rule 4). A robot moves between networks; its
  host key does not. `RobotIdentity.hardwareID` is nil on the simulator, so callers pass `deduplicationKey`.
- **The pinned key is stored as its OpenSSH text line**, not as an opaque blob:
  `String(openSSHPublicKey:)` ⇄ `NIOSSHPublicKey(openSSHPublicKey:)` is a documented round-trip, and a layout that
  belongs to a dependency has no business in a Keychain item.
- **`KeychainSSHCredentialStore` stores username and password only.** Host and port are the session's business; a
  remembered address is exactly the mistake rule 4 warns about, so `credentials(forRobot:)` returns an empty host
  for the caller to fill.
- **The fingerprint needs no SwiftNIO.** The base64 field of an OpenSSH line _is_ the SSH wire encoding, which is
  what OpenSSH hashes, so `HostKeyFingerprint` is Foundation plus one SHA-256 — and its tests use vectors from
  `ssh-keygen -lf`, not from this code. A trailing comment is dropped, or one key would pin as two.

## Defaults, and why they are only defaults

Reachy Mini Wireless ships with OpenSSH enabled, user `pollen`, password `root`. `SSHCredentials.defaultUsername`
offers the username as a prefill. Never assume the password: a user who takes the advice to change it must still be
able to connect. Say so on the screen.

## Testing

`Tests/ReachySSHTests` covers only what is pure — fingerprints, the mode→kind mapping, permission rendering, path
joining, error classification. There is **no integration test against a live SSH server**, and the cheap way to
exercise the real actor is to enable Remote Login on the Mac and point the app at it: that is a genuine OpenSSH
server for the price of a checkbox. `PreviewFileSystem` (in `Preview/`, `#if DEBUG`, the same convention as
`ReachyKit/Preview/PreviewRobotClient`) is what previews and the UI model's tests run against; it records calls in
order, so "did it even ask?" is assertable. It is here rather than in `ReachyTestSupport` so no other test target
links SwiftNIO.

`PreviewFileSystem.brokenPersonality()` is the 2026-08-07 incident as a fixture: `user_personalities/Test_Ru` in
the old four-file format with no `profile.md`. Keep it broken — it is the state the feature exists for.

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(files): close abandoned SSH sessions and stop hiding listing failures

Four findings from review, three of them real.

- **A refused listing left the loading overlay up for good.** `refresh()` set
  `hasListed` only on success, and the screen keys its full-bleed "Reading the
  folder…" overlay off that flag — an overlay that covers the very error row the
  failure had just filled in. A refusal is an answer, so it sets the flag too.
  Worth noting why no reference caught this: `Robot files — permission refused`
  injects `hasListed: true`, so the preview rendered the error correctly while
  the real code path could not reach that state. The test does what the
  reference could not.
- **Abandoned sessions leaked a TCP connection each.** `SSHClient` has no
  `deinit` and `close()` is the only thing that shuts its channel, so a model
  released on navigating away left a live connection to the robot behind, one per
  visit, for as long as the app ran. `RobotFilesModel.deinit` now disconnects.
- **The Keychain was read on every render.** `NavigationLink { … }` builds its
  destination eagerly and `RobotFilesScreen` adopts only the first model into
  `@State`, so the initialiser's `SecItemCopyMatching` was a main-thread XPC
  round trip whose result was thrown away every time but once. It moved to
  `start()`, behind a flag rather than an `isEmpty` check — someone who clears
  the field because the robot's password changed must not have the old one put
  back under them.
- **A bare mode made every entry `.other`.** `kind(mode:longname:)` read the
  `S_IFMT` bits without checking any were set, so a server sending `0o755`
  rather than `0o040755` produced `isDirectory == false` for directories and left
  the tree unopenable. OpenSSH sends the full `st_mode`, so the robot never hits
  it; a wrapper trimming the field would. It now falls back to `longname`, which
  is what the nil case already did.

Two corrections to the review itself. The proposed fix for the synchronous
`Data(contentsOf:)` in `fileImporter` — wrapping it in `Task { }` — does not
move it off the main actor, because a task created in a `@MainActor` context
inherits that isolation; `pickedFile(at:limit:)` uses `Task.detached` and also
caps the size, since a picked 2 GB file was a memory problem before it was a
responsiveness one. And the host-key comparison mismatch cannot misbehave —
every stored property of `HostKeyFingerprint` derives from the key line in one
initialiser — but two spellings of one question do invite drift, so both sites
now use `==`.

`RobotFilesModel.swift` went over the 400-line limit, so the error mapping and
the state vocabulary moved to files of their own. What could not move is
anything writing a `private(set)` member, the setter being private to the
declaring file — which is also why the `#if DEBUG` preview factory stays put.

906 tests, 303 snapshot references unchanged, both app builds, lint clean.
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git push 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
CI зелёный на `366abe4` — все три джоба.

## Разбор ревью: 7 замечаний, 5 верных

| # | Замечание | Вердикт |
|---|---|---|
| Листинг с ошибкой → вечный спиннер | **HIGH, верно** | исправлено + тест |
| Утечка SSH-сессий при уходе с экрана | **HIGH, верно** | `deinit` + тест |
| Keychain читался на каждый рендер | верно | перенесено в `start()` |
| `mode` без битов S_IFMT → всё `.other` | верно | откат на `longname` + тест |
| Чтение файла на главном потоке | проблема верна, **фикс не работает** | исправлено иначе |
| Сравнение host key рассогласовано | поведение идентично | привёл к одному оператору |

**Две поправки к самому ревью.**

Предложенное `Task { Data(contentsOf:) }` **не уводит работу с главного актора** — таск, созданный в `@MainActor`-контексте, наследует эту изоляцию. Нужен `Task.detached`, что я и сделал; заодно добавил лимит размера, потому что выбранный файл на 2 ГБ — это в первую очередь проблема памяти, а не отзывчивости.

Рассогласование в сравнении host key сломаться не может: все три поля `HostKeyFingerprint` выводятся из одной строки ключа в одном инициализаторе, так что `!=` и сравнение `openSSHPublicKey` тождественны. Но замечание про две формулировки одного вопроса справедливо, поэтому я свёл к `==` в обоих местах — в обратную сторону от предложенной.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Самое ценное здесь — что баг с вечным спиннером не поймал ни один из 303 эталонов, и причина в моём же превью.** `Robot files — permission refused` инжектит `hasListed: true`, то есть рендерит состояние, до которого настоящий код дойти не мог. Картинка выглядела правильной и «удостоверяла» ошибку, которая в жизни была бы накрыта спиннером. Это второй случай за сессию, когда инъекция состояния для превью маскирует поведение — первый был с Advanced ниже сгиба. Вывод общий: **снапшот проверяет рендер состояния, но никогда не проверяет, что состояние достижимо.** Достижимость — работа теста модели.

**`private(set)` — это файловая граница, а не типовая.** Когда файл модели перевалил за 400 строк, выяснилось, что вынести можно только то, что не пишет `private(set)`-свойства: `describe` уехала, а `report` вернулась, потому что пишет `lastError`. Та же причина держит `#if DEBUG`-фабрику превью в файле модели — что репозиторий уже знал и записал в `AGENTS.md`, но я прочувствовал только сейчас.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Состояние:** PR [#22](https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift/pull/22), три коммита, CI зелёный. 906 тестов, 303 эталона не сдвинулись.

Два открытых пункта, оба честные: **SSH-путь по-прежнему ни разу не исполнялся** против живого сервера, и **на телефоне билд от коммита до этих правок** — телефон заблокирован, запуск отклоняется. Скажите, когда разблокируете, переставлю.
